FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 431
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Matthew Hammett
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 03/03/2026
House Bill 431 as introduced could increase receipts to the State General Fund, county funds,
and municipal funds by an undetermined amount dependent upon the amount of carbon dioxide
stored in underground wells that would be taxed at 20% of its gross value under this bill, to be
distributed as follows:
 50% to the State General Fund;
 50% to the county in which the carbon is stored, provided that if the carbon is stored within
municipal corporate limits, 50% of county proceeds shall be distributed to the municipality.
This bill could also increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Revenue to
adopt rules to administer the provisions of this bill.

FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 431
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Matthew Hammett
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 03/12/2026
House Bill 431 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means General Fund could increase
receipts to the State General Fund, county funds, and municipal funds by an undetermined
amount dependent upon the amount of carbon dioxide injected for storage in underground wells
that would be assessed a fee of $0.18 per ton of carbon dioxide injected under this bill, to be
distributed as follows:
50% to the State General Fund; and
50% to the county in which the carbon is stored, provided that if the carbon dioxide is stored
within municipal corporate limits, 50% of county proceeds shall be distributed to the
municipality.

Further, this bill could increase receipts to the Underground Carbon Dioxide Storage Facility
Trust Fund by an undetermined amount dependent upon the amount of filing fees collected from
the $20,000 annual monitoring fees established by this bill.
This bill would also provide all fees provided by the bill are subject to periodic CPI adjustment.
